title: Candidate
description: FROZEN CONTRACT for the Inteltion HR MVP. Every API 'data' payload for a single candidate matches this shape exactly. NULL RULE: there are no nulls anywhere - a missing string is "", a missing number is 0, a missing array is []. Every property is always present. Mirrored in code as backend/app/schemas.py (Pydantic) and shared-contracts/status.ts (TypeScript). ROUND 4 (v2.0.0, 18 Sep 2026): adds `before_rejected_status` and `possible_duplicate_of`; DEPRECATES `hr_comment` / `line_manager_comment` - both are now read-only and computed, and comments live in comment-log-schema.json. v2.1.0 (19 Sep 2026): BREAKING - the status 'CV rejected' is renamed 'Rejected'. Every frontend literal and every stored row must be updated; backend/alembic/versions/0002_rename_cv_rejected.py migrates existing databases. v2.2.0 (19 Sep 2026): BREAKING - the upload response gains `needs_review[]`. A CV that soft-matches an existing candidate no longer auto-creates; it waits for a human create-or-update decision. See pending-upload-schema.json. v2.3.0 (round 5, 30 Sep 2026): additive - adds `owner_account_id` and `owner_name` (candidate ownership; see ownership-schema.json). Not breaking on its own, but note: the round-4 `feature/backend` <-> `main` contract gap (see FRONTEND_CONTRACT_GAPS.md) is still unresolved - this round adds to that same divergence rather than narrowing it.

candidate_id.description: 7-digit zero-padded running number assigned by the backend in creation order (e.g. '0000001', '0000042'). Read-only. Ignored if sent in a PUT/upload body.

email.description: Not format-validated on extraction; PUT rejects a value with no '@'.

location.description: PROPOSED ADDITION vs the Member 3 doc schema - present in the master plan and CapstoneMeeting.md. City, country / 'Remote'.

hr_comment.description: DEPRECATED (round 4, removed next round). READ-ONLY: the text of the newest live comment with comment_type='hr', computed by the server. Writing it in a PUT body is ignored. Read GET /api/candidates/{id}/comments and POST there instead - see comment-log-schema.json.

line_manager_comment.description: DEPRECATED (round 4, removed next round). READ-ONLY: the text of the newest live comment with comment_type='line_manager', computed by the server. Writing it in a PUT body is ignored. See comment-log-schema.json.

raw_text_snippet.description: Debug only. First ~500 chars of parsed CV text.

status.description: THE canonical pipeline status list. This array is the single source of truth: the backend loads it from this file at startup (backend/app/statuses.py) and shared-contracts/status.ts is generated from it. Defaults to 'New' on upload. BREAKING in v2.1.0: 'CV rejected' was renamed to 'Rejected' - they always meant the same thing, and 'rejected at which stage' is answered by `before_rejected_status` instead. Rejected states are, by convention, any value ending in 'rejected'.

before_rejected_status.description: READ-ONLY, server-managed. The pipeline status held immediately before the candidate entered a rejected state, so HR can see 'rejected at interview' vs 'rejected at CV screening'. '' when the candidate is not currently rejected. Ignored if sent in a PUT body. POST /api/candidates/{id}/restore moves the candidate back to this value. The full transition log is GET /api/candidates/{id}/status-history.

upload_status.description: Read-only. File/extraction lifecycle, SEPARATE from `status` (HR pipeline). 'Processing' during extraction, 'Done' when ready, 'Failed' on error, 'Not Uploaded' for a draft with no CV yet. A candidate can be deleted only when this is NOT 'Processing'.

resume_url.description: Read-only. Link to the stored original file ('' if none).

resume_filename.description: Read-only. Original filename of the NEWEST CV version ('' if none). Every earlier version is still kept - GET /api/candidates/{id}/resume-versions.

possible_duplicate_of.description: Read-only. candidate_ids this record MIGHT duplicate, from an exact phone match or full_name + applied_position, computed at upload time when no email match was possible. [] most of the time. The backend never auto-merges on this - HR decides, because a false merge loses a person's history with no undo.

owner_account_id.description: Round 5. Read-only here - set once, to whoever imported the CV, at creation. Re-uploads and the pending-upload 'update' resolution never change it. Changed only via POST /api/candidates/{id}/transfer-ownership (the current owner, or an admin). '' for the rare row that could not be attributed to any account. See ownership-schema.json.

owner_name.description: Round 5. Read-only. Live lookup of owner_account_id's current full_name, NOT a snapshot - unlike comment author_name, a renamed owner's new name shows immediately. '' when owner_account_id is ''.

candidateSummary.title: CandidateSummary
candidateSummary.description: Shape returned by GET /api/candidates (list view). Derived from Candidate.

before_rejected_status.description: Read-only. See the top-level field - included here so the Kanban can render a 'rejected at X' badge without fetching the full candidate.

top_skills.description: Up to 5 skill names, flattened from skills[].skill.

owner_account_id.description: Round 5. See the top-level field. Pass this value back as ?owner_account_id= on GET /api/candidates for a 'my candidates' filter.

owner_name.description: Round 5. Live lookup, not a snapshot - see the top-level field.

uploadResponse.title: UploadResponse
uploadResponse.description: `data` of POST /api/candidates/upload. BREAKING in round 4: `updated` is new. A file whose extracted email matches an existing candidate updates that record instead of creating a second one, so the UI must distinguish '3 new candidates added' from '1 added, 2 existing records updated' - otherwise HR will not realise a record was overwritten. BREAKING in v2.2.0: `needs_review` is new - those files are NOT in the database yet and need a create-or-update decision before they count for anything. `count` = created.length + updated.length, and deliberately EXCLUDES needs_review.

created.description: Candidates that did not exist before.

updated.description: Existing candidates whose extraction-owned fields were overwritten by a new CV. status / before_rejected_status / applied_position / location / candidate_id / created_at and all comments are preserved.

needs_review.description: Files that stopped for a human decision: no exact email match, but a plausible soft match (same phone, or same name + position). NOTHING was written to the candidates table for these. The UI must prompt per item - 'update the existing record' or 'create a new candidate' - and call the matching endpoint in pending-upload-schema.json. Ignoring this array means the CV is silently never imported.

failed.description: Per-file errors. A bad file fails only its own entry; if EVERY file fails the endpoint returns 400 instead.

candidate_id.description: Present only when a row was created before the failure.

responseEnvelope.title: ResponseEnvelope
responseEnvelope.description: Every endpoint returns this. success: {data: <payload>, error: null}. failure: {data: null, error: <message>}.
